chunks: From him, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, who said: Zurkan ibn Ahmad narrated to me, Muhammad ibn 'Asim narrated to me, from Abu al-Sahhari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: 'A man feeds one sheep or two sheep to sacrifice them.' He said: 'I do not like that.' I said: 'A man buys a lamb and a sheep, their fodder falls from here and from there, so when the time comes they have become fat, so he slaughters them.' He said: 'No, but when that time comes, let him enter the market of the Muslims, buy from them, and slaughter them.'

key_terms.لَا أُحِبُّ ذَلِكَ: I do not like that (a common juristic expression indicating dislike or recommendation against)
key_terms.يُضَحِّيَ: to offer a sacrifice (specifically Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for acquiring an animal for Eid al-Adha sacrifice according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) discouraged pre-feeding specific animals for Eid al-Adha to prevent the potential negligence of keeping them in one place until the last moment, which might lead to defects or delay. Instead, he recommended purchasing fresh animals from the market at the time of sacrifice, a practice that ensures the animal's suitability and reflects the spirit of readiness and immediacy in worship. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on both the physical condition of the sacrificial animal and the spiritual intention behind the act of Udhiyah.
